questions.stem: To study the human body, we use several branches of anatomy. Which of the following correspond to topographical anatomy?
options: The study of morphological variations in human races
The analytical study of the morphology of separate organs
The study of the relations of the organs

questions.stem: For the study of the descriptive, topographic, and functional anatomy of the human body, we use the following reference axes: the body axis, the hand axis, and the foot axis. What are the characteristics of the body axis?
options: An axis that passes through the center of gravity of the body

questions.stem: The transverse plane is a reference anatomical plane that divides the body into two parts. What are its characteristics?
options: It is parallel to the ground
It is perpendicular to the ground
It divides the body into two parts: right and left
It divides the body into two parts: cranial and caudal

questions.stem: Dynamic coordinate systems indicate the direction of movement; each movement occurs in a plane relative to an axis. What is the axis and what is the plane of medial rotation?
The systems of the human body are grouped into three main categories: the life and relationship system, the reproductive system, and the nutrition system. What are the nutrition systems?
Cartilage is a strong yet elastic tissue. It lacks blood vessels and is classified into three types. What are the characteristics of hyaline cartilage?
options: It constitutes the means of joint adaptation

questions.stem: Bones are rigid, hard structures in the human body and make up the human skeleton. What are the characteristics of the appendicular skeleton?
options: It is made up of the spine
It attaches to the axial skeleton
It is made up of the skeleton of the thoracic limb

questions.stem: The surface of bones is irregular, with cavities and projections that can be articular or non-articular. Which of the following correspond to non-articular projections?

The hip bone (os coxae) is a bone that makes up the bony pelvis and is embryologically formed by the joining of three bony parts: the ilium, ischium, and pubis. Which of the following correspond to its lateral surface?
The bony pelvis is divided into two sections by the pelvic inlet: the greater pelvis and the lesser pelvis. Which of the following represent the boundaries of this pelvic inlet?
options: Behind, the promontory of the sacrum
Laterally, the arcuate lines of the hip bones

questions.stem: The femoral head is a spheroid articular projection located at the proximal epiphysis. Which of the following are the characteristics of this femoral head?
options: It is covered with fibrous cartilage

questions.stem: The axis of the femoral neck forms an angle of inclination of 125° to 130° with that of the diaphysis. Which of the following angles corresponds to coxa valga?
The tibial plateau represents the base of the proximal epiphysis of the tibia and it articulates with the femoral condyles. Which of the following anatomical elements constitute it?
options: The superior lateral tibial articular surface

questions.stem: The distal epiphysis of the tibia articulates inferiorly with the talus. Which of the following are the articular surfaces of this epiphysis?
options: The medial superior tibial articular surface
The superior lateral tibial articular surface
The articular surface of the medial malleolus
The articular surface of the lateral malleolus

questions.stem: The proximal tibial epiphysis is a quadrangular pyramid with a base and four faces, each with several tuberosities. What are the tuberosities of this proximal epiphysis?
Flexion and extension of the hip joint occur around a transverse axis that passes through the center of the femoral head. What is the range of motion of the hip joint with the knee extended?
The knee joint is a weight-bearing joint equipped with ligaments and tendons that provide the stability necessary for standing and walking. What joints make it up?

The knee joint is a weight-bearing joint. It is equipped with ligaments and tendons that provide the stability necessary for standing and walking. The central pivot is a strong ligament of this joint. What are its characteristics?
options: It is made up of the cruciate ligaments
It is made up of the collateral ligaments
It is made up of the patellar ligament
It ensures the anteroposterior stability of the knee
It ensures lateral stability of the knee

questions.stem: Knee flexion is the act of bringing the back of the leg towards the back of the thigh. What is the range of passive flexion for a flexed hip?
The subaponeurotic skeletal muscle:
options: It is a muscle located between the fascia and the skin
It is a muscle found in the pharynx and larynx
It is an involuntary muscle with rapid contractions

questions.stem: From an insertion point perspective, a skeletal muscle:
options: Must have a starting point (usually fixed) and an ending point (usually mobile)
It can be inserted onto the skin, like the palmaris brevis muscle
It can attach to the fascia, like the cricothyroid muscle
It can insert onto cartilage, like the abductor hallucis muscle
It can attach to the bone, like the brachioradialis muscle

questions.stem: The muscular fascia:
options: Is also called the covering aponeurosis
It is a fibrous groove delimiting the osteofibrous canals with the bone

questions.stem: The inferior surface of the clavicle presents:
options: The groove of the subclavius muscle, in the middle
The trapezoid line, which gives attachment to the ligament of the same name
The conoid tubercle, where the conoid ligament attaches

questions.stem: The lateral angle of the scapula supports several anatomical structures such as:
options: The neck of the scapula which supports the coracoid process
The coracoid process which gives attachment to the coracoclavicular ligament
The supraglenoid tubercle, which provides insertion for the triceps brachii muscle
The scapular notch where the suprascapular artery and nerve pass
The glenoid cavity which faces laterally

questions.stem: Among the protrusions (projections) of the diaphysis of the humerus, the following are mentioned:
options: The crest of the lesser tubercle
The crest of the greater tubercle

questions.stem: The medial border of the radius:
options: Is also called the interosseous border
Separates the two surfaces, anterior and lateral, of the radius
It continues on both epiphyses of the radius
Faces the lateral border of the ulna
Provides attachment to the forearm interosseous membrane

questions.stem: The coronoid process of the ulna bears the following anatomical structures:
Among the carpal bones, the following are mentioned:
options: The scaphoid bone located laterally on the proximal row
The trapezoid bone belongs to the proximal row
The pisiform bone which articulates with the lunate bone
The capitate bone is located in the middle of the proximal row
The hamate bone is located medially on the distal row

questions.stem: The wrist is composed of the following joints:
The antebrachial articular surface of the radiocarpal joint:
options: It is a convex elliptical surface
It has a major transverse axis
It is formed of two parts: the carpal articular surface of the radius, and the radioulnar articular disc
It is divided into three thirds: 1/3 lateral and 2/3 medial
It articulates with the four carpal bones of the proximal row

questions.stem: Which passive ligaments of the radiocarpal joint terminate on the lunate?
options: The radial collateral ligament of the carpus
The ulnar collateral ligament of the carpus

questions.stem: The forefoot is composed of the following joints:
options: The interphalangeal joints of the foot

questions.stem: The eversion movement of the foot is the result of the combination of three foot movements. Which ones?
The trochlea of the talus:
options: It is a large protrusion, articulating with the leg
It articulates medially with the articular surface of the medial malleolus
It articulates laterally with the fibula via a comma-shaped articular surface

questions.stem: The elbow joint is a complex joint that unites the humerus, ulna, and radius. This joint has several articular surfaces. What is the position of the capitulum?
options: It occupies the outer surface of the coronoid process
It occupies the perimeter of the head of the radius
It is located on the lateral and distal part of the humerus
It is located in the medial and distal part of the humerus
It is located on the lateral and proximal part of the humerus

questions.stem: The elbow has three palpable bony landmarks posteriorly: the lateral epicondyle, the medial epicondyle, and the olecranon. Which of the following correspond to these landmarks?
Synovial joints are characterized by the presence of a joint cavity, a synovial membrane, and bone surfaces covered with articular cartilage. The latter is characterized by:
options: The same thickness in all joints
Its lesions are reversible with medical treatment
Its degeneration is responsible for osteoarthritis
It covers the epiphyses of the long bones

questions.stem: The adaptive mechanisms are fibrocartilaginous structures that exist in cases of joint incongruity and are interposed between the bone surfaces:
options: They play a role in joint mobility
They are interposed between the capsule and the synovium
They are essential for joint stability
They are never the site of lesions

questions.stem: The sternocostoclavicular joint unites the medial end of the clavicle with the sternal manubrium and the first costal cartilage:
options: It's a saddle joint with an articular disc
It is an arthrodial (plane) joint with an articular disc
It's a joint that allows for slight gliding movements
It's a slippery space with a serous bursa
The articular surfaces are joined by a thick capsule and two ligaments

questions.stem: The coracohumeral ligament is a strong ligament that originates from the lateral border of the coracoid process. What is its termination?
options: By two bundles, one on the greater tubercle and the other on the lesser tubercle
By three bundles on the greater and lesser tubercles and on the anatomical neck
By two bundles, one on the anatomical neck and the other on the surgical neck
By a single bundle on the bicipital groove
By a single bundle on the surgical neck
